title: AI could build my RPG character, but getting attached to it took more than fixing the eyes
author: oddgustudio
selftext:
I'm building Wobble Kingdom with AI coding assistance. I wanted the appeal of a slightly hopeless-looking adventurer, inspired by TABS, in a fantasy RPG. The first characters looked more like they were waiting for a group photo.



The frustrating part was that a change could look better close up and still feel wrong at the gameplay camera distance. I started with the eyes and eyelids, then had to revisit body proportions and the resting pose. Having a working model wasn't the same as having a character I wanted to spend a game with.



This is a short look back at those early versions, not the latest build. Where would you draw the line between an intentionally awkward character and one that just looks unfinished?



Video with English subtitles: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jR1lJy-dhkI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jR1lJy-dhkI)



I'm the developer. AI assists development and the Korean narration. No TABS assets are used.
